subject: Scope of statements
notes: Rule: a single imperative statement not contained in another is terminated by 'a) any element that follows the exhaustion of the statement's syntax, or b) the next-encountered statement-name, or c) a separator period' (cite.py --check 14.5.3.3 -> OK §14.5.3.3 1) a)). Mechanism: sentence : statement+ DOT, each statement rule consumes exactly its own syntax, so the next statement keyword (b), the DOT (c), or a following element such as ELSE (a) ends it. Probes: 'DISPLAY "T8 A" DISPLAY "T8 B" MOVE 1 TO A DISPLAY A.' -> three separate statements (sc1 T8); every sentence in sc1/sc4 ends at its period. Reserved statement names cannot be absorbed as operands (§8.9 reservation), so no adversarial operand/statement-name collision exists. No spec-derived test targets this rule specifically: test-needed. probe dir out/probe/scope-of-statements (sc1/sc4/sc5, pinned cobol.exe; sc1 identical output at --std 85/2002/2014/2023, sc4 at 85 and 2023) [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (explicit/implicit scope termination is COBOL-85 surface; Annex E records no change to 14.5.3)]
